source.exact_title: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline on the Evaluation and Management of Candidates for Kidney Transplantation
source.source_type: evidence-based global clinical practice guideline with evidence profiles and supplemental methods appendices
source.citation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Kidney Transplant Candidate Work Group. Transplantation. 2020;104:S1-S103.

source_files.role: supplemental appendix B, IOM standards concurrence

source.evidence_search: Systematic searches last conducted August 2017; additional evidence review through May 2019.
source.substantive_main_range: S1-S83 plus references S84-S97 and disclosure appendix S98-S103

semantic_batches.scope: scope, methods, grading, search reproducibility, IOM process limitations

evidence_profiles.title: Kidney transplantation vs waitlisting
evidence_profiles.finding: Transplantation was generally superior to remaining waitlisted across age groups and obesity; evidence in HIV-positive candidates was sparse and very low certainty.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-emptive transplantation vs transplantation after dialysis
evidence_profiles.finding: Registry studies gave inconsistent results depending on whether pre-emptive transplantation was compared with transplantation within one year of dialysis or with any post-dialysis transplantation.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-transplant predictors of post-transplant mortality
evidence_profiles.quality: High to very low by predictor
evidence_profiles.finding: Age, diabetes, cardiovascular disease and peripheral vascular disease were associated with mortality in registry analyses; BMI and several other predictors were less consistent.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-transplant predictors of graft loss
evidence_profiles.quality: Moderate to very low by predictor
evidence_profiles.finding: Morbid obesity and hypoalbuminemia were associated with graft loss in some analyses, while age and underlying kidney-disease effects were inconsistent.

evidence_profiles.title: Predictors of other post-transplant outcomes
evidence_profiles.finding: Sparse registry data linked prior skin cancer to post-transplant malignancy and age, hypertension, obesity, and HCV to new-onset diabetes after transplantation.

evidence_profiles.title: Psychosocial testing
evidence_profiles.finding: SIPAT was not consistently associated with mortality or graft loss; some measures showed possible associations with nonadherence or graft failure.

evidence_profiles.title: Nonadherence and retransplantation
evidence_profiles.finding: Patients retransplanted after graft loss attributed to nonadherence had outcomes similar to retransplanted patients whose prior graft was lost for other reasons; there was no comparison with patients not retransplanted.

evidence_profiles.title: Glucose tolerance testing
evidence_profiles.finding: Impaired glucose tolerance or fasting glucose before transplantation predicted new-onset diabetes after transplantation; OGTT had poor sensitivity but high specificity for that outcome.

evidence_profiles.title: Treatments to prevent kidney-disease recurrence
evidence_profiles.finding: Evidence was unclear for plasmapheresis preventing recurrent FSGS, while eculizumab appeared to reduce recurrence and graft loss in high-risk aHUS.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-transplant nephrectomy for UTI or BK-associated nephropathy
evidence_profiles.finding: Post-transplant survival was high after nephrectomy for vesicoureteral reflux, graft loss was similar, and BK-associated nephropathy could recur after nephrectomy.

evidence_profiles.title: Tuberculosis testing
evidence_profiles.finding: Pre-transplant tuberculin skin testing did not consistently predict post-transplant tuberculosis.

evidence_profiles.title: Tuberculosis treatment duration
evidence_profiles.finding: Post-transplant TB was uncommon among patients who received 3-6 months of treatment, but the evidence base was limited.

evidence_profiles.title: Hepatitis B treatment with lamivudine
evidence_profiles.finding: About half of hemodialysis patients achieved long-term viral elimination; mortality signals favored treatment but were underpowered.

evidence_profiles.title: Transplant outcomes in patients with HIV
evidence_profiles.finding: Available data did not clearly establish whether HIV status altered post-transplant mortality or graft loss.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-transplant vaccination
evidence_profiles.finding: HBV and measles vaccination before transplantation could preserve post-transplant immunity; three or four HBV doses appeared more effective than two in limited data.

evidence_profiles.title: Cancer screening
evidence_profiles.finding: Screening detected cancers and precancerous lesions, but the studies were indirect and did not establish effects on patient-important outcomes.

evidence_profiles.title: Cancer recurrence risk after pre-transplant treatment
evidence_profiles.finding: Recurrence risk varied markedly by cancer type; selected treated RCC/VHL cohorts had post-transplant outcomes similar to patients without RCC.

evidence_profiles.title: Cardiac revascularization before transplantation
evidence_profiles.finding: Patients who underwent kidney transplantation after CABG had better survival than patients who remained without transplantation, but direct evidence that pre-transplant revascularization improves transplant outcomes was limited.

evidence_profiles.title: Pre-transplant echocardiography
evidence_profiles.finding: Several echocardiographic abnormalities, including reduced systolic function and pulmonary hypertension, were associated with post-transplant death or graft loss.

evidence_profiles.title: Carotid artery testing
evidence_profiles.finding: Imprecise evidence suggested that pre-transplant carotid stenosis was not clearly associated with post-transplant stroke or TIA.

evidence_profiles.title: Intracranial imaging in ADPKD
evidence_profiles.finding: Evidence did not directly show that screening improves outcomes; aneurysm prevalence was appreciable, but rupture, mortality, age effects, and interval change were inconsistent.

evidence_profiles.title: Thrombophilia testing
evidence_profiles.quality: Moderate to very low by outcome
evidence_profiles.finding: Most thrombophilia factors did not predict death or graft loss; antiphospholipid syndrome without adequate anticoagulation was the main clinically important risk signal.

evidence_supplement.handling: Evidence-profile results were used for SEA evidence reconciliation. They remain secondary reports and were not promoted to primary-study LiteratureAtoms.

main_inventory.handling: Search yield: 45,914 citations from 32 searches, 762 full-text articles retrieved, 190 included studies.
Reevaluation protocol after graft loss due to nonadherence, including patient response, causal assessment, multidisciplinary review, treatment, and relisting pathway.
Algorithm for evaluation and HCV-treatment timing in kidney transplant candidates.
Systematic review topics and screening criteria.
Hierarchy of critical and important outcomes.
Work products by guideline topic, including search yield, included studies, and evidence-profile availability.
Study-quality classification, GRADE evidence framework, benefit-harm balance, recommendation nomenclature, recommendation-strength determinants, and COGS reporting checklist.
Initial and follow-up screening of viral and nonviral pathogens.
Routine vaccinations for kidney transplant candidates.
Cancer-screening recommendations for the general population and transplant candidates.
Recommended waiting times between cancer remission and kidney transplantation.

visuals_and_tables.visual_qa: Key main figures/tables, all 22 evidence-profile summary pages, representative search-strategy pages, and all six Appendix B pages were rendered and visually inspected.

references.handling: The canonical main-guideline bibliography was extracted once. Evidence-profile PMIDs and table-local citations were used for evidence reconciliation and were not duplicated as a second bibliography.

coverage_decisions: Every numbered formal guidance statement in the summary was mapped. Intentional cross-references that repeat an earlier recommendation were not atomized twice.

Recommendation 10.5.2.4.2 was split into two atoms because the two clauses have different evidence grades. Recommendation 10.7.5 was split into six vaccine-specific atoms because each bullet is separately graded.
Underlying primary-study results summarized by KDIGO were not converted to primary-study atoms.
The 634-entry bibliography was extracted separately and not atomized.
Biographic disclosures were inspected at source level but were not atomized person by person.
source_integrity_and_method_findings: Appendix B explicitly records several IOM systematic-review standards that were not fully met, including no analytic framework or standard clinical-question format, no public/peer-reviewed protocol, no independent search-strategy peer review, and one extractor with a second reviewer checking.
Appendix B also records incomplete handling of intellectual conflicts of interest and limited patient/consumer participation procedures compared with IOM guideline standards.
No external verification or update search was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
